projects.name: Solar + Energy Storage on Garage
projects.description: Install 5-7 solar panels on south-facing garage roof face (20x12 ft, ~2-2.8 kW) plus battery storage. Solar = standalone ROI investment (~5yr payback at $0.42/kWh). Battery = generator alternative (no lot space for generator). 30% federal ITC applies to both when paired.
projects.notes: DESIGN: South garage face only. 5 portrait panels = 2.0 kW; 7 mixed = 2.8 kW. ~3,200-4,500 kWh/yr production (20-26% offset). All-in after ITC: solar ~$9-10k, battery ~$9-10k. VENDORS: Sunergy (sunergy.com) — EnergySage 2026 CA Installer of Year, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door. NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com) — Diamond Certified, 35yr, San Mateo County, 40yr warranty. Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy) — online only. AVOID: Sunrun.

tasks.title: Analyze energy usage and size system
tasks.notes: 17,178 kWh/yr at $0.42/kWh avg. Target: 5-7 panels south garage face (20x12 ft) = 2-2.8 kW. ~5yr payback after ITC.

tasks.title: Research and shortlist solar installers
tasks.notes: Shortlist: Sunergy (sunergy.com, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door), NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com, Diamond Certified, San Mateo County), Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy, online only). Avoid Sunrun.

tasks.title: Contact installers for quotes
tasks.notes: Spec: south garage face (20x12 ft, 5-7 panels, ~2-2.8 kW), paired battery (Enphase IQ or Powerwall 3), detached garage sub-panel interconnect. Ask each for: $/W, panel brand, inverter type, battery spec, warranty, timeline, ITC total. Request free shade/LIDAR analysis.

tasks.title: Compare quotes and select installer
tasks.notes: Prefer Enphase microinverters over string inverter. Compare $/W, battery spec, warranty, timeline. 30% ITC on full system incl. battery.

tasks.title: Confirm ITC timing — credit files in year PTO is granted
tasks.notes: 30% federal ITC on Form 5695. Claimed in tax year Permission to Operate granted by PG&E. Battery qualifies only when solar-paired. Plan install timing accordingly.

insights.summary: The persistent 18-21 device count paired with zero camera motion on a Thursday morning strongly suggests a large, stationary gathering in a camera-blind zone, or a potential camera/network anomaly; verify if extended guests are present or if cameras require maintenance.

The consistent presence of 18-21 mobile devices combined with zero camera motion on a Thursday afternoon strongly indicates a large indoor gathering (likely 10+ guests or a remote work/study session) rather than normal family routine, confirming the earlier medium-severity flag.

A sustained high device count (18-21) on a Thursday mid-morning, paired with zero camera activity, strongly suggests either a sick day/remote learning for the kids or a group of quiet guests. The recent drop to 18 at 11:03 may indicate someone left or devices entered sleep mode, so confirming the day's schedule is recommended.

The drop to 17 connected devices at 08:33 aligns with typical school departure time, but the complete lack of camera motion during this window suggests either the family exited via a non-triggered route or the cameras are offline, warranting a quick sensor status check.

The steady decline in connected devices from 24 to 17 between 08:14 and 08:33 strongly indicates the family is departing for school and work, aligning with a typical Thursday morning routine. The remaining 17 devices likely represent stationary smart home equipment or items left behind, which is normal but worth monitoring if the count stabilizes unusually high.

The stable presence of 25-26 devices combined with zero camera activity and normal sleep metrics indicates a quiet, fully occupied home likely hosting guests in non-camera zones, with no signs of distress or unusual movement.

The baseline of 20-22 devices aligns with a fully occupied smart home, but the sudden jump to 26 connected devices in the last 10 minutes without corresponding camera activity suggests either unmonitored arrivals or routine IoT synchronization; a quick verification would confirm if guests arrived or if it's just late-night connectivity.

The persistent 20-22 connected mobile devices paired with zero camera activity throughout the evening strongly suggests the home is unoccupied, indicating the presence network data is likely unreliable (possibly counting IoT devices or tracking phones left behind) and warrants verifying camera status or confirming the family's whereabouts.

The consistent 20-22 device count confirms the home is occupied during prime evening hours, but the complete lack of camera activity points to a monitoring gap (e.g., cameras in privacy mode, offline, or network issue) rather than an empty house. This matters because it leaves the home unmonitored despite high occupancy, warranting a quick system status check.

The persistent 20-22 connected devices paired with zero camera activity throughout the evening strongly suggests the security cameras are offline, disabled, or masked, creating a monitoring blind spot while the network remains active. Verify camera status to ensure the home is being properly watched.
